newsitem.title: USA: GM stock pressured by PaineWebber downgrade.
newsitem.headline: GM stock pressured by PaineWebber downgrade.

text.p: General Motors Corp shares were pressured Tuesday by PaineWebber Inc's downgrade of GM stock to neutral from attractive, analysts said.
A PaineWebber spokesman confirmed the downgrade, issued Monday, but details were not immediately available. GM shares were off 1-5/8 to 56-5/8.

Burnham Securities analyst David Healy said the PaineWebber downgrade is probably the biggest factor affecting GM shares. Goldman Sachs on Tuesday removed GM from its Private Client Focus Portfolio and added International Business Machines Corp., according to a Goldman source.

In addition, GM was hit with a third strike early Tuesday at its Warren, Ohio electrical wiring harness plants. The strike could force a broad shutdown of GM's North American operations because the Warren operations produce critical electrical parts used in nearly all GM vehicles.

But one analyst, who spoke on condition of anonymity, noted that Wall Street has typically supported GM's willingness to sustain costly strikes by its unions in order to gain local agreements that allow it to improve its competitiveness.
"A strike is not worth two points on the stock," he said. "These stocks are valued based on what happens next year and the year after."
